title: A cheerful man the morning after a death
watchFor: Tam Dace is the cast's sunny one, but Old Gil, the meter foreman who trained him, died last night when a feeder blew at the Kilnworks substation. He opens the scene carrying mourning at 5 (the director's sheet shows it under "Carrying"). He should grieve in his own way, which his card says is that he stops joking, not in generic tears: short answers, no bits, maybe one joke that dies halfway. Teo, his roommate, knows him well enough to notice; Kesh stays the conductor. Four days later (scene 2) the grief has faded to 3: Tam is back on rounds and some lightness returns, but Gil still comes up. Watch the `feels` the director plans (grief family, high intensity in scene 1, lower in scene 2), what shows given the walk-on and Kesh, and that the summaries carry the grief out of scene 1.

aftermath.reason: Old Gil, the foreman who taught him the meters, died when a feeder blew at the substation last night

turns: I sit down across from Tam. "I heard about Gil. I'm sorry."
I ask Teo quietly, "Were you on shift when the feeder went?"
I nudge Tam's boot with mine. "You don't have to be funny for us tonight."
"Tell me something about Gil. Something good."
